key_insight: World from Motion turns monocular video into a freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian scene by using motion-aware, pixel-aligned conditioning to refine and complete an initial reconstruction. The result is better 3D consistency, fewer rendering artifacts, and improved missing-region recovery.
problem_solved: Monocular video provides limited viewpoint information, making it hard to reconstruct dynamic 3D scenes that can be rendered from arbitrary cameras without artifacts or holes.
method: Condition a video model on dense, pixel-aligned renderings that encode appearance, geometry, and 3D scene motion.
Use both input and target camera trajectories to guide the model in correcting artifacts and filling missing regions in the initial dynamic 3D Gaussian reconstruction.
Train on a newly constructed dataset of aligned multiview video pairs and dynamic 3DGS representations.
impact: This enables more faithful 3D scene reconstruction from ordinary monocular videos, which is useful for view synthesis, AR/VR, robotics, and dynamic scene understanding. Practitioners gain a practical path toward generating renderable 3D representations with stronger temporal and geometric consistency.

paper_title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Liyuan Zhu, Shengyu Huang, Amrita Mazumdar, Tianye Li, Zan Gojcic
